newsitem.title: UK: Boeing feared McDonnell bid for Hughes - paper.
newsitem.headline: Boeing feared McDonnell bid for Hughes - paper.

text.p: Boeing Co moved swiftly to buy competitior McDonnell Douglas Corp because it feared that McDonnell Douglas was about to bid for the defence operations of Hughes Electronics Corp, the Financial Times reported today.
Boeing and McDonnell Douglas announced a $13.3 billion deal to merge on December 15.
McDonnell was understood to be planning to submit a bid for the Hughes operations by an auction deadline of December 13, the paper said.
The owner, General Motors Corp, is seeking between $8 billion and $10 billion for Hughes Electronics, it said.

Boeing chief executive Philip Condit hastened Boeing's bid after he only 10 days earlier had heard about McDonnell's likely bid, which would have made McDonnell a less attractive acquisition, the Financial Times said.
Condit told Wall Street analysts on Monday that Boeing would not make a bid for the Hughes business.
